Question: Does the platform support sample-based auditing with configurable confidence intervals, stratified by risk level?
Response: Yes. Statistical QC is implemented through the Fleet Manager agent and Foundry Evaluators. The Fleet Manager can configure sample-based auditing: (1) Random sampling — 10% of completed workflows are flagged for human review. (2) Stratified by risk — high-risk workflows (high-value invoices, senior hires) have higher sampling rates. (3) Configurable confidence intervals — the sampling rate adjusts based on desired statistical confidence. The Fleet Manager composes the QC queue on the Control Plane: selected workflows are presented to the operator with full context for review. QC results (human confirms agent decision, or human overrides) feed back into quality metrics and threshold calibration. This is not a pre-built statistical QC product — it is implemented through Fleet Manager skills that encode the sampling logic and Foundry Evaluators that score quality.
Key Technologies: Fleet Manager agent (sampling logic), Foundry Evaluators (quality scoring), Control Plane (QC queue)

Question: Can independent evaluator agents audit worker agents using separate criteria, models, and data; provably independent (no shared memory)?
Response: Yes. Our architecture naturally supports this through domain-scoped Hosted Agents. The Fleet Manager agent is a separate Hosted Agent (fleet-manager@wpp) with its own Entra identity, its own model configuration, and read-only access to telemetry — it does not share memory or execution context with the domain agents it monitors. The Fleet Manager evaluates domain agent outputs using separate criteria (defined in Fleet Manager skills) and can use a different model than the domain agents. Independence is provable: separate Entra identity, separate Hosted Agent container, separate model deployment, read-only access (cannot modify domain agent state). Additionally, Foundry Evaluators run as separate evaluation pipelines with their own model configurations — they evaluate agent outputs independently of the agent that produced them. For maximum independence: configure the auditing evaluator to use a different model provider than the audited agent.
Key Technologies: Fleet Manager (independent auditor), separate Entra identity, separate model deployment, Foundry Evaluators (independent pipeline)

Question: Describe continuous behavioural monitoring against baselines with alerts for unusual tool usage, escalation changes, quality shifts, cost spikes.
Response: Continuous behavioural monitoring operates at three layers. (1) APIM AI Gateway: monitors per-agent, per-tool usage patterns. Statistical baselines are established from normal operation. Anomalies trigger alerts: unusual tool call frequency, unexpected tool access patterns, abnormal token usage. (2) Foundry Evaluators: continuous evaluation on production traffic against quality baselines. Task adherence monitoring detects behavioural drift from the agent's defined purpose. Quality score degradation triggers automated alerts. (3) Fleet Manager: reasons about fleet-wide behavioural patterns. Detects: unusual escalation rate changes, cost spikes, quality shifts across workflow types, tool usage pattern changes. Alerts surface on the Control Plane with context and recommended action. All alerting integrates with Azure Monitor for notification channels (email, Teams, PagerDuty) and Microsoft Sentinel for security-focused anomaly detection.
Key Technologies: APIM anomaly detection, Foundry Evaluators (behavioural baseline), Fleet Manager (fleet-wide patterns), Azure Monitor, Microsoft Sentinel
POC Demo: POC1: Simulate cost spike — show anomaly detection triggering Fleet Manager alert on Control Plane with root cause analysis.

Question: Can outputs be clearly marked as agent-generated, human-generated, or human-reviewed; configurable per client and regulatory context?
Response: Yes. All outputs carry provenance metadata. (1) Agent-generated: outputs produced by agentic loops are marked with the agent identity, skill version, and model used. OTEL spans provide full provenance chain. (2) Human-reviewed: outputs that passed through HITL approval carry the approver's identity and timestamp. The action ledger distinguishes between autonomous actions and human-approved actions. (3) Human-generated: actions taken directly by humans (not through an agent) are attributed to the human's identity. Configurable per context: skills can be configured to add explicit transparency markings to outputs (e.g. 'This shortlist was generated by AI and reviewed by [HR BP name]' or 'This offer letter was generated by AI'). Regulatory context: EU AI Act requires transparency for automated screening decisions — the compliance skill adds required disclosures. Client context: different WPP clients may have different transparency requirements, configurable in the workflow metadata.
Key Technologies: OTEL provenance metadata, action ledger (audit attribution), skill-configurable transparency markings, Entra identity attribution
POC Demo: POC2: Show transparency marking on screening output — 'AI-generated shortlist, reviewed by [HR BP]' with full provenance chain.

Question: If a primary model provider goes down, can agents fail over to alternative models with acceptable quality? Describe the model-abstraction layer and cross-model eval baselines.
Response: Yes. APIM AI Gateway provides the model-abstraction layer with built-in failover. Configuration: (1) Primary model endpoint (e.g. Azure OpenAI GPT-4.1). (2) Fallback model endpoint (e.g. alternative Azure OpenAI deployment in another region, or a different model from the Foundry catalog). (3) APIM health checks detect primary model unavailability and automatically routes to fallback. GHCP SDK is model-agnostic — the agentic loop works with any model from the Foundry catalog (1900+ models). Skills can specify acceptable model alternatives. Cross-model eval baselines: Foundry Evaluators run quality assessments on both primary and fallback models. The fallback model is pre-validated to meet minimum quality thresholds for each skill. If fallback quality is below acceptable levels, the Fleet Manager surfaces a degradation alert on the Control Plane and can increase HITL oversight until the primary model recovers.
Key Technologies: APIM AI Gateway (model failover), Foundry model catalog (1900+ models), Foundry Evaluators (cross-model baseline), Fleet Manager (degradation alerts)
POC Demo: POC1: Simulate primary model endpoint failure — show APIM failover to alternative model, Fleet Manager notification of degraded mode, quality comparison on Control Plane.

Question: Describe platform-level circuit breakers preventing cascading failures. What is brown-out mode (partial work, queue for humans)? How does automatic failover to human queues work?
Response: Circuit breakers operate at multiple levels. (1) APIM AI Gateway: circuit breaker policies detect repeated failures on model endpoints or MCP tool calls. After configurable failure threshold, APIM opens the circuit — subsequent calls return immediately without hitting the failing service. APIM retries periodically to detect recovery. (2) Durable Functions: retry policies with max attempts prevent a single failing phase from blocking the workflow indefinitely. After max retries, the phase enters exception state. (3) Fleet Manager: detects cascading failure patterns across the fleet (e.g. Workday API down affecting all finance workflows) and alerts the operator proactively. Brown-out mode: when a dependency is degraded (not fully down), the architecture degrades gracefully. Agentic loops can proceed with cached data or partial results. The Fleet Manager switches affected workflows to increased-HITL mode — more decisions route to human queues. Automatic failover to human queues: when circuit breakers trip, pending work items are composed with full context and routed to the appropriate operator's PA for manual processing. The Control Plane shows which workflows are in brown-out mode.
Key Technologies: APIM circuit breakers, Durable Functions retry limits, Fleet Manager (cascading failure detection), brown-out mode (increased HITL)
POC Demo: POC1: Simulate Workday API degradation — show circuit breaker tripping, brown-out mode activation, affected workflows routed to Finance BP queue.
